extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to the American Economic Review; coeditors, editors, and referees handling AER submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and peer‑reviewing guidelines for manuscripts submitted to the American Economic Review, covering review model, editor/coeditor assignment and recusal rules, data and code requirements, disclosure and AI policies, comments/replies, and item ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single‑blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts submitted to the American Economic Review undergo single‑blind peer review—the name of the author is revealed to the referee(s), while the referee(s) remain anonymous to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a manuscript is received, the editor assigns it to a coeditor or to themselves (in the role of coeditor) to oversee the review process and to make a publication decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coeditor assignment on submission
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission, authors have the opportunity to request one or more specific coeditors to handle their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor usually follows such requests if they are consistent with the criteria for assigning papers, including field of expertise of the coeditor, equalization of workload, and adherence to conflict‑of‑interest rules. Once assigned, papers are handled by the designated coeditor throughout the decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor/Coeditor right to return without external review
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor and coeditors reserve the right to return manuscripts to authors without referee review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to return a manuscript without review is based on several considerations, including expected probability of meeting the standards of the AER, breadth of topic, and interest to the AER audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coeditor consultation before first revise‑and‑resubmit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before giving a first revise‑and‑resubmit decision, the coeditor will consult a second coeditor of their choosing for input.

rubrics_metrics.name: AEA data editor review prior to final acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers conditionally accepted by the coeditor then undergo a review by the AEA data editor to determine whether the paper complies with the AEA’s Data and Code Availability Policy and Data Legality Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review occurs prior to final acceptance/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of coeditor in published article
rubrics_metrics.description: When papers are accepted and published, the coeditor in charge is identified in the acknowledgement footnote of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coeditor in charge recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Coeditors are recused from papers involving current colleagues at the same institution (regardless of department), as well as graduate students at the same institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional recusal grounds: coauthors of current papers or papers published less than two years ago; untenured students they advised; a coeditor at a different journal who is currently handling one of the coeditor’s own papers or has accepted one of the coeditor’s own papers in the past two years; family members; and any other close personal or professional relationship which, in the coeditor's opinion, creates a conflict (e.g., coauthor of a current project, former tenured student still close to, advisee of author, etc.). It is the responsibility of the coeditor to identify a conflict of interest to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting coeditor recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Consulting coeditors are recused from consulting on papers involving colleagues in the same department and from papers involving untenured students they advised under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: can consult on papers from authors in different departments in the same institution; recused from consulting on papers involving untenured students they advised if these students have graduated less than three years ago or if the paper was part of the student’s dissertation; recused from papers involving a family member; and must disclose any other close personal or professional relationship that creates a conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling submissions by coeditors or the editor (guest editor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted by a coeditor or the editor are handled by a guest editor employing appropriate confidentiality procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guest editor has full editorial discretion. If the paper is submitted by a coeditor, the editor invites a guest editor. If the paper is submitted by the editor, a coeditor invites a guest editor. Current coeditors or the current editor cannot serve as guest editor. If possible, the guest editor is drawn from former editors or coeditors of AEA journals or from members of the board of editors. The guest editor's name is identified in the acknowledgement footnote of the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Comments and Replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted to the AER should provide a substantial and general‑interest contribution beyond what could be known from the original article and other articles in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may be summarily rejected by the editor or the assigned coeditor or sent for review to the author of the original article and likely to other reviewers. If the author of the original paper submits a Reply, it will be sent to the author of the Comment and generally to other reviewers. There is no automatic right to Reply; for a Reply to be accepted it must provide substantive and material discussion of the issues. For comments that do not meet the standard for formal publication, the coeditor may offer posting on the article’s landing page as an e‑comment/e‑reply/e‑amendment, depending on substance and merit and reactions of authors/reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of order of items in each issue (lead article criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which papers appear in each issue is determined by the editor in consultation with the coeditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead article is selected based on factors such as the importance of the questions it addresses, the quality of analysis, the innovation over the literature, and the clarity of presentation. Subsequent articles generally follow the order of acceptance, with occasional deviations (e.g., grouping related articles). Any comments and replies are printed after regular articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Policy for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting papers for peer review, all authors must provide disclosure statements identifying potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors have nothing to disclose, they must explicitly state this. Disclosure statements should also include whether IRB approval was obtained for the project, and if not, state the reason(s). For published papers, a brief summary of potential conflicts should appear in the acknowledgement footnote. The entire disclosure statement is posted with the paper on the journal's website. (See full Disclosure Policy.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in manuscripts and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) software, such as chatbots or other large language models, may not be listed as an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If AI software was used in preparation of the manuscript, including drafting or editing text, this must be briefly described during the submission process so editors understand how AI was used. Authors are solely accountable for, and must thoroughly fact‑check, outputs created with the help of AI software. Reviewers: the reviewer's report is expected to reflect their own careful reading and evaluation of the paper; any use of AI during the review must be disclosed in the reviewer's cover letter and must be limited to tools that guarantee that the manuscript will not be used for training AI models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Legality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All data used in papers published in journals of the American Economic Association should be legally acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coeditor in charge may reject the paper if some or all of the data were not legally obtained. (See full Data Legality Policy, effective July 2023.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Code Availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to acceptance, authors of papers that contain empirical work, simulations, or experimental work must provide the data, code, and other details of the computations sufficient to permit replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the AEA’s Data and Code Availability Policy; these materials are reviewed by the AEA data editor as part of the conditional acceptance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCT registration policy for field experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: All work involving field experiments must be registered with the AEA RCT Registry prior to submission for publication.
